title: 11th Sitting of Second session of 2026
summary: The sitting, chaired by the Deputy Speaker, opened with a question session in which 11 members asked Education Minister Dr. Ismail Shafeeu about delayed school building projects, teacher allowances, school attendance and parent-teacher fundraising. The President's nomination of an ambassador to Belgium and the EU was sent to the Foreign Relations Committee, and the government's bill amending the Waste Management Act had its first reading and a preliminary debate. The Majlis then approved, by 64 votes to 0 each time, the committee report on non-resident ambassadors to South Africa, the Czech Republic, Mauritania and Kenya.

items.title: Attendance of the sitting
items.outcome: 34 present, 7 on leave, 4 on official travel announced

items.title: Questions to the Minister of Education, Higher Education and Skills Development, Dr. Ismail Shafeeu
items.outcome: 11 members asked questions and the minister answered each; no vote

items.title: President's letter on appointing an ambassador to Belgium and the European Union
items.outcome: referred to the Foreign Relations Committee

items.title: First reading of the bill to amend the Waste Management Act (Act 24/2022), submitted on behalf of the government by Ibrahim Shifaz (Ungoofaaru)
Preliminary debate on the bill to amend the Waste Management Act (Act 24/2022)
items.outcome: debated; members given more time to study the bill

items.title: Foreign Relations Committee report on non-resident ambassadors to South Africa, the Czech Republic, Mauritania and Kenya
items.outcome: debated, then approved in three votes of 64-0

speakers.name: Dr. Ismail Shafeeu
positions: As Education Minister he answered each question on school projects, giving progress and target dates for the works raised.
Said 210 school projects are under way, with over 1,200 classrooms built, at a total cost of about MVR 2.98 billion.
Said schools must now send daily attendance to the ministry, which will act on pupils not attending school.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Falah
positions: Asked how far the Arabiyya school building has progressed and why the breakfast programme was stopped.
Backed the waste law amendments and urged members to read the amendments before criticising them.
Supported the ambassador appointments and said ambassadors will keep being appointed as part of foreign relations.

speakers.name: Mauroof Zakir
positions: Asked why work on the new Kamadhoo school building has not begun and when pupils could use it.
Asked about the allowance for teachers who completed a master's certificate years ago.
Asked when work on the Kihadhoo Donfanu school building will start.

speakers.name: Hussain Ziyad
positions: Asked when long-delayed classroom work at Vaikaradhoo Atholhu Madharusa and the Neelaidhoo school building will start.
In the ambassador debate, said he supports the committee report but questioned what benefit the public gets from appointing ambassadors.

speakers.name: Ahmed Azaan Marzooq
positions: Asked for an update on the Hithadhoo Sharafuddin school hall project.
Asked about the pledge to fit air conditioning in Addu schools and why some classrooms still lack power.

speakers.name: Ameen Faisal
positions: Asked when work on the Feydhoo and Goidhoo school projects will start and finish, given pledges made to residents.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Nazil
positions: Asked whether goods under the Hunan Province and Addu City Council agreement have been handed to the ministry for Sharafuddin school.
Asked when the multi-purpose hall at Sharafuddin school will be finished.

speakers.name: Hassan Mufeed Abdul Gadir
positions: Asked what steps the ministry is taking about children who do not attend school.

speakers.name: Hussain Sameer
positions: Asked when the Rasdhoo school building will be completed and services start.
Asked whether parent-teacher association fundraising has been halted and what is being built on the Gazee school land.

speakers.name: Ahmed Xamyr
positions: Asked how many school building projects the government is running and how much they cost.

speakers.name: Ahmed Didi
positions: Asked about the Maradhoo school hall work handed to a contractor after the President's visit.
Asked when the Irushaadhiyya school building will be ready for use.

speakers.name: Abdul Gafoor Moosa
positions: Asked about the long-delayed Naavaidhoo school hall work.
Asked when classroom construction at Hanimaadhoo school will begin.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Shifaz
positions: Presented the government's bill to amend the Waste Management Act to clarify agency roles, ban waste imports and fix enforcement gaps.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Didi
positions: Thanked the sponsor and backed the amendments, citing overlaps between agencies and dumping in protected zones and at sea.

speakers.name: Abdulla Rifau
positions: Supported the bill as a way to remove overlaps between agencies and asked the committee to add penalties for illegal dumping.

speakers.name: Mohamed Fazeel
positions: Supported the amendments, saying they remove overlaps between the three agencies, and raised dumping and roadside waste.

speakers.name: Hassan Zareer
positions: As committee rapporteur, presented the Foreign Relations Committee report finding the nominees for South Africa, the Czech Republic, Mauritania and Kenya eligible.

decisions: The President's letter on appointing an ambassador to Belgium and the European Union was referred to the Foreign Relations Committee.
The bill to amend the Waste Management Act (Act 24/2022) was read for the first time and debated at the preliminary stage.
Dr. Hala Hameed (H. Meenaz) was approved as non-resident ambassador to the Republic of South Africa.
Aminath Abdulla Didi (G.Dh. Thinadhoo, Gulzaar) was approved as non-resident ambassador to the Czech Republic.
Ameen Javud Faisal (H. Athireege) was approved as non-resident ambassador to the Islamic Republic of Mauritania and the Republic of Kenya.
The next sitting was set for Wednesday 8 July 2026 at 9:00 am.

votes.what: Appointment of Dr. Hala Hameed as non-resident ambassador to South Africa (93 members, 65 present, 33 needed)
Appointment of Aminath Abdulla Didi as non-resident ambassador to the Czech Republic (93 members, 65 present, 33 needed)
Appointment of Ameen Javud Faisal as non-resident ambassador to Mauritania and Kenya (93 members, 65 present, 33 needed)
